# What CI and contributors install for the quality-gate toolchain, with `--require-hashes`: the
# pins in requirements-dev.in and every dependency they pull in, each held to the sha256 of every
# file PyPI listed for that version when this was generated. A version pin alone admits a file
# added to the release later (PyPI lets a maintainer add files to an existing release, never
# replace one), and pip prefers a more specific wheel; a hash admits only the files that were
# already there. Every file is listed, not only one runner's, so each CI Python and platform and a
# contributor's machine all find their wheel.
#
# Hash checking is all-or-nothing per pip command, so install this beside requirements-release.txt
# (the hashed copy of requirements-validation.txt), never beside an unhashed file:
#
#     python3 -m pip install --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes \
#         -r requirements-release.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
#
# Generated, never edited by hand. After changing a pin in requirements-dev.in, rerun
#
#     uv pip compile requirements-dev.in --universal --python-version 3.12 \
#         --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --exclude-newer <two weeks before today>
#
# `--universal` resolves for every platform rather than the machine that runs it; 3.12 is the
# oldest Python the gate runs. `--exclude-newer` (an ISO date) keeps a dependency the bump adds at
# least two weeks old, the rule the direct pins follow. Replace everything below this header with
# its output, and check the hashes against the sha256 digests PyPI publishes at
# https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json. test_release_workflow.HashPinnedInstallTest fails
# while a pin in requirements-dev.in differs from its pin here.
